security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, placeholder callback URLs, and normal webhook or customer identifiers. I confirmed the hardcoded Stripe secret-key examples as unsafe guidance and added semantic findings for webhook secret handling and manual verification. No prompt injection, malicious exfiltration, or shell execution intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Load Stripe API keys from environment variables or a secret manager. Add a warning not to commit test or live keys.
Use an environment variable for endpoint_secret and document rotation for webhook signing secrets.
Prefer stripe.Webhook.construct_event. If manual verification remains, validate the timestamp, signed payload, expected scheme, and replay tolerance.

content.value_statement: Payment integrations require secure checkout, webhook handling, and subscription logic. This skill guides Stripe implementations with practical patterns, testing advice, and operational safeguards.
actual_capabilities: Explains hosted Checkout, Payment Intents, Setup Intents, and subscription flows.
Provides Python examples for Checkout Sessions, Payment Intents, subscriptions, and customer portals.
Shows webhook signature verification, event handling, and idempotent processing patterns.
Covers customer payment methods, refunds, disputes, and billing portal sessions.
Lists Stripe test card scenarios and payment flow testing guidance.
limitations: It does not provide a deployable application or complete database schema.
Examples are primarily Python, so other languages require adaptation.
Stripe API versions and compliance rules must be checked against current Stripe documentation.
Production systems still need secret management, monitoring, and legal review.

use_cases.title: Launch Subscription Billing
use_cases.description: Plan products, prices, checkout sessions, payment confirmation, and cancellation handling for a SaaS subscription flow.

use_cases.title: Harden Webhook Processing
use_cases.description: Review webhook event coverage, signature verification, idempotency, retries, and fulfillment timing.

use_cases.title: Manage Payment Operations
use_cases.description: Design refund, dispute, customer portal, and saved payment method workflows for support teams.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Payment Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a first Stripe integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which Stripe payment flow fits a simple one-time purchase. Include required backend steps, frontend steps, and testing checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Subscription Checkout
prompt_templates.scenario: Builder adding recurring billing to a SaaS product.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hosted Checkout subscription flow for my SaaS product. Include products, prices, success handling, cancellation handling, and webhooks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Webhook Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Stripe webhook plan for missed events, idempotency gaps, error handling, and customer access updates.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Marketplace Payments
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced team designing a multi-party payment system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for a marketplace using Stripe Connect, saved payment methods, refunds, disputes, and compliance checkpoints.

output_examples.input: A request to choose between hosted Checkout and Payment Intents.
output: Recommended flow: hosted Checkout for the first release.
Reason: it lowers PCI scope and supports fast payment validation.
Next steps: create a session, configure callback URLs, and verify webhooks.

output_examples.input: A request to harden webhook processing.
output: Verify signatures with the Stripe SDK.
Store processed event identifiers before fulfillment.
Retry failed work with clear alerts and audit logs.

output_examples.input: A request to plan subscription billing.
output: Model products and prices before implementation.
Use default incomplete subscriptions for SCA support.
Handle subscription updates, cancellations, and invoice payment results.

best_practices: Use hosted Checkout when custom card handling is not required.
Verify webhook signatures and process events idempotently before fulfillment.
Keep Stripe keys and webhook secrets in managed secrets, not source files.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on client redirects to mark payments as complete.
Do not store raw card data or send it through your backend.
Do not copy placeholder keys or callback URLs into production.

faq.question: Does this skill build a complete Stripe app?
faq.answer: No. It gives implementation patterns and review guidance for your existing app.

faq.question: Can it help with subscriptions?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers products, prices, subscriptions, invoices, customer portals, and lifecycle events.

faq.question: Does it reduce PCI scope?
faq.answer: It recommends hosted Checkout and Stripe.js patterns that keep raw card data away from your server.

faq.question: Can it review webhook handling?
faq.answer: Yes. It can check event coverage, signature verification, idempotency, retries, and access updates.

faq.question: Does it include testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It references test mode, test cards, failed payments, and 3D Secure scenarios.

faq.question: Should I still read Stripe documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. Use current Stripe documentation for API version details, compliance requirements, and regional payment rules.
